method: Recompute coarse/fine synthetic D8 drainage from rounded V2.4 DEM, with fixed zero-coast Priority Flood and steepest downslope path. Filter eligible coast outlet cells by >=27 (coarse) and >=108 (fine) upstream cells. Greedy maximum-area anchored clustering using 8-connected coastal Dijkstra shortest-path <= R. For each R, one-to-one nearest-anchor cross-grid matching within Euclidean 30 drawing units. For R30 paired mouth sectors, classify every valid fine land cell by its own fine-grid coastal outlet sector and by the sector of the coarse-grid cell that spatially contains it; calculate paired-sector catchment overlap IoU, recall and precision.
notes: The R30 grouping exactly reproduces the 24 coarse/25 fine/24 paired baseline from V2.7.
Distance-only mouth matches can have low drainage-basin overlap and should not be promoted to official river identities.
The catchment overlap test uses the fine-grid mask as area sampling; within matched sectors not all fine valid land cells contribute to eligible large mouths.
The geographic coastline and DEM are unconfirmed and without physical length scale; all results are synthetic.
Sensitivity radii are chosen for method exploration and do not prescribe a real river-mouth width.
Stable means only >=50% synthetic catchment IoU in this one model under this test, not geological confirmation.
